definition_zh: 乐意地；自愿地；心甘情愿地
definition_en: in a way that shows you are ready and glad to do something, without being forced
core_image: 有人还没说完请求，听的人已经把袖子卷起来，笑着往前走了一步
scene: 搬家那天，她一喊，几个邻居没等把话讲完就卷起袖子下楼帮忙。They willingly carried the heavy boxes up four floors without a word of complaint.
sceneCN: 这里 willingly 是「乐意地」（第 1 个义项：自愿且痛快地做某事）；句意为他们心甘情愿地把沉重的箱子搬上四层楼，一句怨言也没有。卷起袖子笑着往前那一步，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: With a glad heart
senses.definition: in a ready and cheerful way, with no sign of being pushed into it
senses.definitionCN: 带着愿意且愉快的心情，没有一点被逼迫的样子
senses.example: They willingly carried the heavy boxes up four floors without a word of complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 他们心甘情愿地把沉重的箱子搬上四层楼，一句怨言也没有。
senses.why: The adverb simply turns the inner readiness of will into the way an action is done.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是把内心那份愿意，变成做事的姿态。

senses.title: Of one's own free choice
senses.definition: by personal choice rather than because a rule or a person demands it
senses.definitionCN: 出于个人选择，而不是因为规定或他人要求
senses.example: She willingly gave up her seat to the old man on the crowded bus.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤的公交车上，她自愿把座位让给了那位老人。
senses.why: Readiness can also mean that nobody asked at all, so the word covers free giving.
senses.whyCN: 愿意有时也意味着根本没人开口，于是这个词也涵盖主动给予。

senses.title: Without payment or pressure
senses.definition: in a way that serves others without expecting money or reward, as in the usual phrase
senses.definitionCN: 在为他人做事而不图钱或回报时使用，常用于固定说法
senses.example: Many retired teachers willingly spend their mornings helping children read.
senses.exampleCN: 许多退休教师心甘情愿地花上午的时间教孩子读书。
senses.why: When readiness costs nothing to the giver, it lines up with the unpaid service of volunteers.
senses.whyCN: 当这份愿意对付出者毫无价钱时，它就与志愿者的无偿服务重合了。

intro.en: Willingly is the adverb built on willing, which comes from the noun will, the faculty of choosing; the root is Old English willan, to wish.
intro.cn: willingly 是由 willing 构成的副词，willing 出自名词 will（选择的能力），词根是古英语 willan（希望、愿意）。

items.en: willan meant to wish or to desire, and willa was the mind that wishes.
items.cn: willan 表示希望、渴望，willa 指那颗愿想的心。

items.en: The adjective willende described someone full of intention, close to today's willing.
items.cn: 形容词 willende 形容一个人满怀意愿，与今天的 willing 很接近。

items.en: The ending shifted to -ing and the word settled as willing, ready to do something.
items.cn: 词尾变成 -ing，这个词固定为 willing，意为愿意去做某事。

items.en: The adverb ending gave willingly, first with the sense of acting by choice.
items.cn: 加上副词词尾得到 willingly，最初表示出于选择而行动。

items.en: Today the word carries a warm tone, suggesting the person is glad rather than merely obedient.
items.cn: 今天这个词带有温和的色彩，暗示此人是高兴的，而不只是顺从。

note.en: The first group holds near twins formed from the same stem, the second holds other adverbs of cheerful consent.
note.cn: 第一组收同根而生、模样相近的词，第二组收其他表示欣然同意的副词。

entries.definition: Ready to do something when asked.
The state of being ready to help.
Doing something with clear reluctance.
Deliberately, often against what is right.
With pleasure, happily.
Willingly and without delay.
By free choice, with no one forcing you.

normalIntro.en: Willingly is will plus -ing plus -ly, so the spelling is only long because it shows the inner choice twice.
normalIntro.cn: willingly 是 will 加 -ing 再加 -ly，拼写之所以长，是因为它把内心那份选择说了两遍。

normal.en: Keep the double l from will, then add ing, then add ly.
normal.cn: 先保留 will 的两个 l，再加 ing，最后加 ly。

normal.en: Willing is the person who says yes with the whole face.
normal.cn: willing 就是整张脸都在说「好」的那个人。

normal.en: The tail -ly marks the manner: how the yes was given.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 标记方式：那个「好」是怎么说出口的。

normal.en: Unwillingly wears the negative hat un-, and drops it to become gladly willing.
normal.cn: unwillingly 戴着否定帽子 un-，摘掉它就变成欣然愿意。

normal.en: Link it to willpower: the same will that decides also drives the glad step.
normal.cn: 把它和意志力联系起来：做决定的那份意志，也推动了愉快的那一步。

abstract.en: A hand reaching for the box before the request is finished.
abstract.cn: 一句请求还没说完，一只手已经伸向那只箱子。

abstract.en: A face opening like a door, no shadow of being pushed.
abstract.cn: 一张像门一样打开的脸，没有半点被推着走的阴影。

abstract.en: Weight accepted as if it were light.
abstract.cn: 重量被接过来，轻得像不存在。

examples.en: He willingly took the night shift so his colleague could go home.
examples.cn: 他自愿接下夜班，好让同事能回家。

examples.en: The children willingly shared their toys with the new boy.
examples.cn: 孩子们乐意把玩具分享给新来的男孩。

examples.en: Nobody promised her money, yet she willingly came every weekend.
examples.cn: 没人许诺给她钱，她却每个周末都心甘情愿地来。

dict_mnemonic.text: will（意愿）+ ing + ly —— 带着意愿去做，就是「乐意地」。

root: 古英语 willan（希望、愿意）→ willa（心意）→ willing（愿意的）→ willingly；同族有 willingness、unwilling。

sensesIntro.en: The word moves from a glad heart to a free choice, and finally to a service that asks for no money.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一颗乐意的心，走到自由的选择，最后走到不求报酬的服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand already reaching out before the request ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：请求还没说完，手已经伸了出去。

branches.en: The glad branch: boxes carried up four floors with a smile.
branches.cn: 乐意分支：笑着把箱子搬上四层。

branches.en: The free branch: a seat given up on a crowded bus.
branches.cn: 自愿分支：在拥挤的车上让出座位。

branches.en: The unpaid branch: retired teachers offering their mornings.
branches.cn: 无偿分支：退休教师献出自己的上午。

branches.en: The manner branch: the adverb colours how the choice is carried out.
branches.cn: 方式分支：副词为选择如何落实涂上色彩。

branches.en: The character branch: a readiness that has become a habit.
branches.cn: 品性分支：愿意已经变成习惯。

intro.en: Willingly is a stack of native pieces: the stem will, the adjective ending -ing and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: willingly 由几个本土成分叠成：词干 will、形容词词尾 -ing 和副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: The stem is native Germanic, so there is no Latin ancestor; the Latin words below are borrowed cousins only.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是本土日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁词只是借入的表亲。

items.meaning: the power to choose or wish
items.example: It is the plain core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词朴素的核心。
它由 will 构成 willing。
它由 willing 构成 willingly。

items.example: The noun keeps the warm tone.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了温和的语气。

items.example: The same stem turns cold here.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词干在这里变得冰冷。

definition_zh: 乐意；意愿；愿意帮忙的态度
definition_en: the quality of being ready and glad to do something when it is needed
core_image: 会场里主持人问谁愿意先上，一排手几乎是同时举了起来
scene: 老师刚问有没有人愿意主持班会，角落里那只手就举得很高。Her willingness to take the difficult task surprised everyone in the office.
sceneCN: 这里 willingness 是「乐意、意愿」（第 1 个义项：随时愿意去做的那种态度）；句意为她愿意接下难办的活，让办公室所有人都吃了一惊。会场里一排手几乎同时举起，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A ready attitude
senses.definition: the state of being ready to do something when asked or needed
senses.definitionCN: 被请求或需要时随时愿意去做的状态
senses.example: Her willingness to take the difficult task surprised everyone in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 她愿意接下难办的活，让办公室所有人都吃了一惊。
senses.why: The ending -ness turns the adjective willing into the trait itself, something you can show or lack.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ness 把形容词 willing 变成这种特质本身，一种你可以表现出来也可以缺少的东西。

senses.title: Eagerness to help others
senses.definition: a friendly readiness that shows itself in small acts of service
senses.definitionCN: 一种友善的愿意，表现在一件件小小的帮助里
senses.example: The neighbours remembered his willingness more than the money he gave.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们记得更多的是他的乐于帮忙，而不是他出的钱。
senses.why: When the readiness looks outward it becomes a social virtue rather than a private mood.
senses.whyCN: 当这份愿意朝向别人，它就成了一种社会美德，而不只是私人的情绪。

senses.title: In business and surveys
senses.definition: the amount of effort or money people say they are ready to give, as in market research
senses.definitionCN: 在市场调查中指人们自称愿意付出的努力或金钱
senses.example: The survey measured customers' willingness to pay for faster delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查测量了顾客为更快的送达付费的意愿。
senses.why: Researchers took the everyday trait and gave it a number, turning a feeling into data.
senses.whyCN: 研究者把这日常特质变成一个数字，把一种感受变成了数据。

intro.en: Willingness is the noun of state built on willing, which grows from will; Old English willan meant to wish.
intro.cn: willingness 是由 willing 构成的状态名词，willing 出自 will；古英语 willan 意为希望、愿意。

items.en: willa was the mind that wishes, and lystan named the desire itself.
items.cn: willa 指愿想的心，lystan 指那份欲望本身。

items.en: The verb willan was a core verb of choosing, used of God, kings and ordinary people.
items.cn: 动词 willan 是选择的核心动词，用于神、君王和普通人。

items.en: willing, ready in mind, gained the noun ending -nesse to name the quality.
items.cn: 愿意的 willing 获得名词词尾 -nesse，用来命名这种品质。

items.en: The spelling settled on -ness and the word spread into law, religion and trade.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 -ness，这个词扩展到法律、宗教和贸易。

items.en: In the last century it became a measured variable in surveys of how much people will pay.
items.cn: 上个世纪它成了调查中可测量的变量，用来衡量人们愿意付多少。

note.en: The first group collects the same family, the second other nouns for an inner drive.
note.cn: 第一组收同一个词族，第二组收其他表示内在驱动的名词。

entries.definition: Ready to help, the adjective behind it.
Doing something with a glad heart.
Reluctance, the lack of this trait.
Stubborn following of one's own wish.
Being prepared and quick to act.
Strong keen desire to begin.
The reason that pushes someone to act.

normalIntro.en: Willingness is the state noun, so its ending -ness works like the -ness in kindness and readiness.
normalIntro.cn: willingness 是状态名词，词尾 -ness 与 kindness、readiness 里的 -ness 一样。

normal.en: Three steps: will, willing, willingness. Each step makes it more abstract.
normal.cn: 三步：will、willing、willingness，每一步都更抽象一点。

normal.en: The -ness ending means the quality itself, as in kindness and darkness.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ness 表示品质本身，如 kindness、darkness。

normal.en: Unwillingness simply pulls the whole word to the opposite side.
normal.cn: unwillingness 只是把整个词拉到相反的一边。

normal.en: Willingness is invisible, so it must be shown by a hand or a step.
normal.cn: 意愿是无形的，所以必须用一只手或一步路来证明。

normal.en: Remember the contrast with ability: ability is what you can do, willingness is what you will do.
normal.cn: 记住与 ability 的对照：ability 是你能做什么，willingness 是你愿意做什么。

abstract.en: A row of hands rising at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 一排手在同一瞬间举起。

abstract.en: Warmth in the voice that says yes.
abstract.cn: 说「好」时声音里的温度。

abstract.en: A door unlocked before anyone knocks.
abstract.cn: 还没人敲门，门就已经开了锁。

examples.en: Her willingness to listen made him talk for an hour.
examples.cn: 她愿意倾听，让他讲了整整一个小时。

examples.en: The company praised the staff for their willingness to work extra hours.
examples.cn: 公司赞扬员工愿意加班。

examples.en: Without your willingness, none of this could have started.
examples.cn: 没有你的愿意，这一切都无从开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: willing（愿意的）+ ness（状态）—— 愿意这种状态，就是「乐意、意愿」。

root: 古英语 willan（希望）→ will → willing（形容词）→ willingness；同族有 willingly、unwillingness。

sensesIntro.en: A private readiness first becomes a visible friendliness, then a number that surveys can measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 私下的愿意先变成看得见的友善，再变成一个调查能测量的数字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand lifted high before the question has quite ended.
core.cn: 核心意象：问题还没完全说完，手已经高高举起。

branches.en: The trait branch: a person ready when the need appears.
branches.cn: 特质分支：需要一出现就准备好的人。

branches.en: The friendly branch: remembered for helping, not for money.
branches.cn: 友善分支：被记住的是帮忙，不是钱。

branches.en: The data branch: willingness to pay, written as a figure.
branches.cn: 数据分支：支付意愿被写成一个数字。

branches.en: The visible branch: what cannot be seen must be shown by acts.
branches.cn: 可见分支：看不见的东西得用行动表现出来。

branches.en: The abstract branch: a feeling turned into a quality and then a measure.
branches.cn: 抽象分支：感受先变成品质，再变成度量。

intro.en: Willingness stacks the native root will with the adjective -ing and the noun -ness; un- flips it to the opposite.
intro.cn: willingness 把本土词根 will、形容词词尾 -ing 与名词词尾 -ness 叠在一起；un- 把它翻成反面。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, so the Latin column lists only borrowed ideas that shade its meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属于日耳曼语，所以拉丁栏只列出给它的意义作注的借入词。

items.example: It is the base of the whole family.
The same root turns to anger.
items.exampleCN: 同一个词根转向了愤怒。

items.meaning: the power to choose by oneself
items.example: The philosophical centre of the stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在哲学上的中心。

definition_zh: 赢；获胜；赢得；争取到
definition_en: to finish first in a contest, or to gain something by effort, skill or luck
core_image: 终场哨响，记分牌上那个数字压过对方，全队冲到场中央抱成一团
scene: 最后一球落地，记分牌上的数字终于反超，队友全冲进场内抱成一团。Our team won the match by a single point in the final second.
sceneCN: 这里 win 是「赢、获胜」（第 1 个义项：在比赛中拿到第一）；句意为我们在最后一秒以一分优势赢下了比赛。终场那一刻记分牌上的反超，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To finish first in a contest
senses.definition: to come first or beat the others in a game, race or fight
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、竞赛或战斗中拿第一、胜过其他人
senses.example: Our team won the match by a single point in the final second.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在最后一秒以一分优势赢下了比赛。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to come out on top, the person or side that stays standing.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是压过对手，留下站着的一方。

senses.title: To gain something by effort
senses.definition: to get something such as a prize, a job or respect through effort or merit
senses.definitionCN: 凭努力或实力得到奖品、职位或尊重
senses.example: She won a scholarship to study abroad after a year of preparation.
senses.exampleCN: 准备了一年之后，她赢得了出国留学的奖学金。
senses.why: A prize follows the contest, so the same verb came to name the thing carried home.
senses.whyCN: 奖品是比赛之后的产物，于是同一个动词也用来命名被带回家的东西。

senses.title: To persuade someone to your side
senses.definition: to succeed in getting people to support or agree with you
senses.definitionCN: 成功让人们支持或同意你
senses.example: His honest answer won over the whole committee.
senses.exampleCN: 他诚实的回答把整个委员会都争取了过来。
senses.why: Support is another kind of contest, and the one who gathers people has again come first.
senses.whyCN: 支持也是一种比赛，把人聚拢过来的那一方同样拿了第一。

senses.title: A victory itself
senses.definition: a success in a game or an election, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 比赛或选举中的胜利，作可数名词
senses.example: The season ended with four wins and two losses.
senses.exampleCN: 这个赛季以四胜两负结束。
senses.why: Once the verb was settled, the noun simply names the event of coming first.
senses.whyCN: 动词定型之后，名词就直接命名那次拿第一的事件。

intro.en: Win is an Old English verb of struggle: gewinnan meant to fight for and gain, and the noun gewin was toil as much as victory.
intro.cn: win 是古英语中表示争斗的动词：gewinnan 意为争取得来，名词 gewin 既指劳作也指胜利。

items.en: winnan meant to labour and to fight, and gewinnan to gain something by struggle.
items.cn: winnan 表示劳作与争斗，gewinnan 表示通过斗争得到某物。

items.en: The noun gewin first stressed toil and hardship more than triumph.
items.cn: 名词 gewin 起初强调的是辛劳与艰苦，多于荣耀。

items.en: The prefix fell away and win became the plain verb of gaining a victory.
items.cn: 前缀脱落，win 成为表示获取胜利的朴素动词。

items.en: Sports and elections made the contest sense dominant, with win the prize following.
items.cn: 体育与选举让竞赛义占了主导，赢得奖品的说法随之而来。

items.en: The sense of winning people over grew as a political and social phrase.
items.cn: 争取人心这一义项作为政治与社会用语发展起来。

note.en: The first group gathers short words that look or sound like win, the second words for succeeding or gaining.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近的短词，第二组收表示取胜或获得的词。

entries.definition: The part of a bird used for flying.
Moving air.
An alcoholic drink made from grapes.
A soft silvery metal or a can.
To defeat an opponent in a contest.
To obtain something wanted.
A great and celebrated victory.

normalIntro.en: Win is one of the shortest verbs in the book, so fix it by its sound rather than by spelling tricks.
normalIntro.cn: win 是全书最短的动词之一，靠声音记比靠拼写技巧更可靠。

normal.en: The three letters sit in the middle of winner and winter alike.
normal.cn: 这三个字母在 winner 和 winter 里都处在中间。

normal.en: Past tense won changes the vowel, like sing to sang.
normal.cn: 过去式 won 换了元音，如同 sing 变 sang。

normal.en: W and V are the only difference between win and vine, so round the lips.
normal.cn: win 与 vine 只差在 w 和 v，所以要收圆嘴唇。

normal.en: Win begins with a W for the raised arms of the victor.
normal.cn: win 首字母 w，像胜利者高举的两条手臂。

normal.en: A win can be one point: the smallest margin still counts.
normal.cn: 一分的优势也算赢，最小的差距也作数。

abstract.en: The sound of the final whistle and a burst of shouting.
abstract.cn: 终场哨响，一片爆发出来的喊声。

abstract.en: A hand raised before the result is even read out.
abstract.cn: 结果还没念，手已经举了起来。

abstract.en: The line of the finish ribbon breaking.
abstract.cn: 终点那条彩带被撞断的弧线。

examples.en: They won the cup for the first time in thirty years.
examples.cn: 他们三十年来第一次赢得了那座奖杯。

examples.en: You cannot win every argument.
examples.cn: 你不可能赢下每一场争论。

examples.en: She won the trust of her students within a month.
examples.cn: 她一个月内就赢得了学生的信任。

dict_mnemonic.text: 首字母 W 像两只举起的手臂 —— 赢了才举起来。

root: 古英语 winnan（劳作、争斗）→ gewinnan（争得）→ 中古英语 win；同族有 winner、winnings。

sensesIntro.en: From hard struggle the word narrows to sport, widens to prizes, then to people won over, and finally becomes the victory itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从艰苦的争斗收窄到体育，再扩展到奖品，再扩展到被争取的人，最后成为胜利本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scoreboard that suddenly turns in your favour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块记分牌忽然转向你这边。

branches.en: The contest branch: a match taken by one point.
branches.cn: 竞赛分支：以一分之差拿下比赛。

branches.en: The prize branch: a scholarship earned through effort.
branches.cn: 奖品分支：凭努力挣来的奖学金。

branches.en: The persuasion branch: a committee brought to your side.
branches.cn: 说服分支：把委员会争取过来。

branches.en: The record branch: four wins in a season.
branches.cn: 记录分支：一个赛季四场胜利。

branches.en: The social branch: winning is done to people as well as against them.
branches.cn: 社会分支：赢既可以对抗人，也可以把人赢过来。

intro.en: Win is a bare Germanic root that takes ordinary endings and forms compounds such as outwin and winnings.
intro.cn: win 是一个光秃秃的日耳曼词根，能接普通词尾，也能构成 outwin、winnings 这类派生词。

latinIntro.en: The root is native and has no Latin source; the Latin entry stands for a borrowed idea only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是本土的，没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目只是借入的概念。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 winning 和 winnings。

items.example: The verb doubled into a slogan.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词叠成了一个口号。

definition_zh: 窗户；窗口；（电脑）窗口；橱窗；可用的时机
definition_en: an opening in a wall fitted with glass that lets in light and air, and a framed area on a screen
core_image: 雨夜里，窗玻璃上挂满水珠，屋里那盏灯把窗框照成一块发亮的方格
scene: 雨下了整夜，玻璃上挂满水珠，屋里那盏灯把窗框照成一个暖黄的方格。Someone tapped softly on the window while the class was reading.
sceneCN: 这里 window 是「窗户」（第 1 个义项：墙上装玻璃、透光通风的开口）；句意为全班读书时，有人轻轻敲了敲窗户。雨夜里那块被灯光照亮的方格，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 窗户；窗口；橱窗；（电脑）窗口；时机

senses.title: The opening in a wall
senses.definition: a hole in a wall filled with glass and a frame, letting in light and letting you look out
senses.definitionCN: 墙上镶玻璃与框的洞口，可以透光也可以向外看
senses.example: Someone tapped softly on the window while the class was reading.
senses.exampleCN: 全班读书时，有人轻轻敲了敲窗户。
senses.why: The old word named the opening itself, before glass was common, so the hole came first and the pane later.
senses.whyCN: 古词命名的是这个洞口本身，那时玻璃还不普遍，所以先有洞后有玻璃。

senses.title: A shop display area
senses.definition: the large glass front of a shop where goods are shown to the street
senses.definitionCN: 商店朝向街道的大玻璃面，用来展示商品
senses.example: The baker arranged the window before sunrise.
senses.exampleCN: 面包师在日出前就摆好了橱窗。
senses.why: A shop window does the same job as a house window, showing what lies inside.
senses.whyCN: 商店橱窗与房屋窗户做的是同一件事：展示里面的东西。

senses.title: A framed area on a screen
senses.definition: a box on a computer screen that holds a separate program or document
senses.definitionCN: 电脑屏幕上承载某个程序或文件的一块方形区域
senses.example: She dragged the window to the second screen.
senses.exampleCN: 她把窗口拖到了第二块屏幕上。
senses.why: Early systems offered a peephole into part of the machine, just as a wall window shows part of the world.
senses.whyCN: 早期系统只是给机器内部开了一个窥视孔，正如墙上的窗只展示世界的一部分。

senses.title: A short period for action
senses.definition: a limited stretch of time in which something can still be done, as in a window of opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 还能做某事的有限一段时间，如「机会之窗」
senses.example: The launch window closes on Friday at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 发射窗口在周五中午关闭。
senses.why: Like a window that is open only briefly, a chance admits action for a little while and then shuts.
senses.whyCN: 正如窗户只开一会儿，一次机会也只在短暂时间里放行行动，然后关上。

intro.en: Window is Old Norse: vindauga joins vindr, wind, and auga, eye, so the word literally means wind-eye.
intro.cn: window 来自古诺斯语：vindauga 由 vindr（风）与 auga（眼）组成，字面意思是「风之眼」。

items.en: vindauga meant a wind eye, an unglazed opening that let air into the hall.
items.cn: vindauga 意为风之眼，是让空气进屋的无玻璃开口。

items.en: The native word for such an opening was eyethurl, eye hole, replaced later by the Norse word.
items.cn: 本土表示这种开口的词是 eyethurl（眼洞），后来被诺斯语词取代。

items.en: The form became windowe, still naming the hole rather than the glass.
items.cn: 形式变为 windowe，指的仍是洞口而不是玻璃。

items.en: The spread of glass panes made the window a bright sheet you look through.
items.cn: 玻璃窗格的普及让窗户变成一片透亮的、可望向外的面。

items.en: Computers borrowed the image for the framed area on a screen, and the idea of a brief period gave a window of opportunity.
items.cn: 计算机借用了这个形象来表示屏幕上的方框，而「短暂时期」的想法带来了机会之窗。

note.en: The first group holds parts of a house near a window, the second words for an opening or a chance.
note.cn: 第一组收房屋里与窗相邻的部位，第二组收表示开口或机会的词。

entries.definition: The coldest season of the year.
A woman whose husband has died.
To make or become wider.
Twisting; a bend in a road.
A hole or gap that lets things through.
A moment that may be used for gain.
A showing of goods or work for others to see.

normalIntro.en: Window comes from wind plus eye, and that picture is the fastest way to keep both the meaning and the double consonants.
normalIntro.cn: window 来自 wind 加 eye，这个画面既能记住意思，也能记住那两个辅音。

normal.en: Wind plus eye: the eye of the wind looking into a room.
normal.cn: wind 加 eye：风的眼睛望进屋子。

normal.en: Two letters after the w: wind, then the rest.
normal.cn: w 之后先写 wind，再写剩下的部分。

normal.en: Both o and w are round, like the round pane of an old cottage.
normal.cn: o 和 w 都是圆的，像老屋那扇圆玻璃。

normal.en: A window lets you look out and lets the wind in, two directions at once.
normal.cn: 窗户让你向外看，也让风向内进，同时朝两个方向。

normal.en: Add sill and you get the ledge below, where cats sit patiently.
normal.cn: 加上 sill 就是下面的窗台，猫在那里耐心地坐着。

abstract.en: Cold glass under a fingertip, colder than the room.
abstract.cn: 指尖下的玻璃冰凉，比屋里更冷。

abstract.en: Rain sliding down while the lamp stays steady behind it.
abstract.cn: 雨往下滑，而灯在它后面稳稳地亮着。

abstract.en: A square of light thrown onto the garden path.
abstract.cn: 一片方块的光落在花园小径上。

examples.en: Please close the window before you go to bed.
examples.cn: 睡前请把窗户关上。

examples.en: From my window I can see the whole valley.
examples.cn: 从我的窗户能看到整个山谷。

examples.en: The singer stood in the shop window, drawing a small crowd.
examples.cn: 歌手站在商店橱窗里，引来一小群人。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词源记忆 · 非词源玩笑
dict_mnemonic.text: wind（风）+ eye（眼）—— 风的眼睛，就是墙上那个进风透光的「窗户」。

root: 古诺斯语 vindauga（风之眼，vindr 风 + auga 眼）→ 中古英语 windowe → window；同族有 windowsill、windowless。

sensesIntro.en: The noun begins as a hole for wind, becomes a bright pane of glass, then a shop display, a screen box and a short season of opportunity.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从让风通过的洞开始，变成一片明亮的玻璃，再变成商店陈列、屏幕方框，最后成了短暂的机会期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lit square of glass in a dark wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：暗墙上的一块发亮方格玻璃。

branches.en: The house branch: knuckles tapping on the classroom glass.
branches.cn: 房屋分支：指节轻敲教室玻璃。

branches.en: The trade branch: goods arranged for the street.
branches.cn: 商业分支：摆给街道看的商品。

branches.en: The screen branch: a document moved to another display.
branches.cn: 屏幕分支：文件被挪到另一块显示屏。

branches.en: The time branch: a launch window that shuts at noon.
branches.cn: 时间分支：正午关闭的发射窗口。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: every later sense keeps the idea of a brief opening.
branches.cn: 隐喻分支：后面每个义项都保留了「短暂开口」的想法。

intro.en: Window is a compound of the Norse words for wind and eye; its endings build a small family such as windows and windowless.
intro.cn: window 是诺斯语「风」与「眼」两个词组成的复合词，它的词尾构成 windows、windowless 等一小族词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Scandinavian, not Latin; fenestra, the Latin word for a window, survives in technical adjectives only.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自斯堪的纳维亚语而非拉丁语；拉丁语的 fenestra（窗）只残留在技术性形容词里。

items.example: The first half of the Norse original.
The second half, an opening that sees.
items.exampleCN: 后半，一只用于看的开口。

items.example: The body part named by its place.

items.meaning: the glass front of a shop
a short period when action is possible
items.example: The opening sense carried into time.

definition_zh: 葡萄酒；酒；果酒；（引申）令人陶醉之物
definition_en: an alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes or other fruit, and by extension anything that intoxicates
core_image: 烛光里一只高脚杯轻轻一晃，深红的液体贴上杯壁又缓缓流回去
scene: 节日的餐桌上，主人给每只高脚杯倒上深红的酒，烛光在杯壁上一晃一晃。A bottle of red wine was opened to celebrate the harvest.
sceneCN: 这里 wine 是「葡萄酒」（第 1 个义项：用葡萄发酵制成的酒）；句意为开了一瓶红葡萄酒来庆祝丰收。烛光里那只杯壁上深红的液体，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The drink of crushed grapes
senses.definition: an alcoholic drink made by letting grape juice ferment, kept in bottles and served with meals
senses.definitionCN: 让葡萄汁发酵而成的酒，装在瓶里，佐餐饮用
senses.example: A bottle of red wine was opened to celebrate the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 开了一瓶红葡萄酒来庆祝丰收。
senses.why: The word first named the vine itself and its juice, and the drink kept the name as the products spread.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指葡萄藤及其汁液，随着这些产物传播，饮品保留了名字。

senses.title: Fruit drinks of the same kind
senses.definition: a similar fermented drink made from other fruits, such as plum, apple or pear
senses.definitionCN: 用李子、苹果、梨等其他水果发酵而成的同类饮品
senses.example: Grandmother made pear wine in a big jar every autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母每年秋天都用大罐子酿梨酒。
senses.why: Once wine meant fermented fruit juice, any fruit could fill the bottle without changing the word.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 wine 表示发酵果汁，任何水果都能装进这只瓶子而不改词。

senses.title: Something that intoxicates
senses.definition: in literature, anything that lifts the mind like drink, such as joy, praise or freedom
senses.definitionCN: 在文学中，指像酒一样让人心飘起来的东西，如喜悦、赞美或自由
senses.example: The wine of first love made him deaf to all advice.
senses.exampleCN: 初恋这杯酒让他听不进任何劝告。
senses.why: The physical warmth of drink became a picture for any strong feeling that carries reason away.
senses.whyCN: 酒带来的那点身体的暖，成了任何强得足以带走理智的情感的样子。

intro.en: Wine is one of Europe's oldest loanwords: Latin vinum stood behind Old English win well before England had vineyards.
intro.cn: wine 是欧洲最古老的借词之一：早在英格兰有葡萄园之前，拉丁语 vinum 就已经站在古英语 win 的背后。

items.en: vinum meant wine, and the word travelled with Roman traders and soldiers.
items.cn: vinum 意为葡萄酒，这个词随罗马商人与士兵一路传播。

items.en: The Germanic tribes borrowed it early, giving forms such as wīn before any written record.
items.cn: 日耳曼部落很早就借入了它，在有文字记录之前就出现了 wīn 这样的形式。

items.en: win named the drink as well as the vine, and appears in laws on trade and feasts.
items.cn: win 既指饮品也指葡萄藤，出现在关于贸易与宴会的法令里。

items.en: Wine settled into the spelling with a silent e, and became the common word at table.
items.cn: 中古英语时拼写加上不发音的 e，成为餐桌上常用的词。

items.en: The word widened to other fruit drinks and lent its warmth to poetry about joy and love.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到其他果酒，并把它的暖意借给了关于喜悦与爱的诗。

note.en: The first group collects spirits and drinks that look or sound similar, the second beverages and the vine.
note.cn: 第一组收形近或音近的酒与饮品，第二组收饮料与葡萄藤相关的词。

entries.definition: The plant that bears grapes.
Air moving across the land.
To come out on top.
A long high complaining sound.
An alcoholic drink made from grain.
Strong distilled drink.
The fruit from which wine is pressed.

normalIntro.en: Wine is short but often confused with vine; the missing first letter is the whole story of a drink made from a vine.
normalIntro.cn: wine 很短，却常与 vine 混；少掉的那个首字母，正是「藤上长出来的酒」的故事。

normal.en: Vine is the plant, and wine is what the plant becomes once pressed.
normal.cn: vine 是藤，wine 是藤被压榨之后变成的东西。

normal.en: The silent e stays quiet, as in fine and line.
normal.cn: 末尾的 e 不发音，和 fine、line 一样。

normal.en: Wine begins with w for the round top of a glass in profile.
normal.cn: wine 以 w 开头，像侧看的杯口那道弧线。

normal.en: One glass of red, two of white: both keep the same short word.
normal.cn: 一杯红的，两杯白的，用的都是这同一个短词。

normal.en: Wine and dine is a rhyme pair you can hear across a dinner table.
normal.cn: wine and dine 是一对押韵的说法，在餐桌那头都听得见。

abstract.en: Deep red liquid clinging to the inside of a glass.
abstract.cn: 深红的液体贴在杯壁内侧。

abstract.en: The small pop of a cork and a burst of dark scent.
abstract.cn: 软木塞一声轻响，涌出一阵深色的香气。

abstract.en: A voice warming up two chairs further along.
abstract.cn: 隔了两个座位，有个人的声音变暖了。

examples.en: They drank a little wine with the fish.
examples.cn: 他们吃鱼时喝了一点葡萄酒。

examples.en: This wine is made from apples rather than grapes.
examples.cn: 这种酒是用苹果而不是葡萄做的。

examples.en: The village has been making wine for four hundred years.
examples.cn: 这个村子酿酒已有四百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: vine（藤）少一个字母、换个首音就成了 wine —— 藤上结的果子酿成「葡萄酒」。

root: 拉丁语 vinum（葡萄酒）→ 日耳曼语借入 wīn → 古英语 win → 中古英语 wine；同族有 vine、winery、winegrower。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the fermented juice of grapes, widens to other fruits, and finally becomes a picture for anything that makes the heart light.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从发酵的葡萄汁开始，扩展到其他水果，最后成为一切让心变轻之物的图画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red liquid turning slowly against a candlelit glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：烛光里深红液体在杯中慢慢打转。

branches.en: The table branch: a bottle opened for the harvest.
branches.cn: 餐桌分支：为丰收开瓶。

branches.en: The orchard branch: pear wine in a big jar.
branches.cn: 果园分支：大罐子里的梨酒。

branches.en: The poetic branch: first love as a drink.
branches.cn: 诗意分支：初恋如一杯酒。

branches.en: The material branch: whatever fruit is available fills the bottle.
branches.cn: 材料分支：有什么果子就装什么瓶子。

branches.en: The extension branch: taste first, then the mind.
branches.cn: 延伸分支：先是舌头，后是心。

intro.en: Wine is a borrowed stem that builds few but useful compounds: winery, wineglass and the verb wine and dine.
intro.cn: wine 是借入的词干，构成的复合词不多但很实用：winery、wineglass，以及 wine and dine 这一说法。

latinIntro.en: The whole word family goes back to Latin vinum, so the Latin column here is the true source, not a cousin.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都回到拉丁语 vinum，所以这里的拉丁栏是真正的来源，而不是远亲。

items.exampleCN: 饮品变成了待客的动词。

definition_zh: 翅膀；机翼；（建筑的）侧翼；派别；（剧场）侧幕
definition_en: the limb a bird or insect uses to fly, and similar flat parts: an aircraft wing, a side of a building or a group inside a party
core_image: 一只鸟在起飞前一瞬把双翅完全张开，风从羽尖下面钻过去
scene: 堤岸上，那只白鸟把双翅完全张开，只一振就离开了栏杆。The bird spread its wings and rose over the river without a sound.
sceneCN: 这里 wing 是「翅膀」（第 1 个义项：鸟或昆虫用来飞的肢体）；句意为那只鸟张开双翅，无声地升到河面上。起飞前双翅完全张开的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 飞；给…装翅膀；（口语）即兴说

senses.title: The limb that lifts a bird
senses.definition: the feathered limb of a bird or the thin flying part of an insect
senses.definitionCN: 鸟的覆羽肢体，或昆虫薄薄的飞行器官
senses.example: The bird spread its wings and rose over the river without a sound.
senses.exampleCN: 那只鸟张开双翅，无声地升到河面上。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the body part, named from the flapping side pieces that a bird carries.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是身体部位，得名于鸟身上那两片扑动的侧片。

senses.title: The lifting surface of a plane
senses.definition: the long flat part sticking out on each side of an aircraft that holds it up in the air
senses.definitionCN: 飞机两侧伸出的长而平的部件，使飞机升空
senses.example: Ice on the wings delayed the flight for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 机翼结冰让航班延误了一个小时。
senses.why: When people built flying machines they took the shape of the bird, and the name came with the shape.
senses.whyCN: 人们造飞行器时借用了鸟的形状，名字也跟着形状一起搬了过来。

senses.title: A side part of a building
senses.definition: a part of a large building that sticks out from the main block
senses.definitionCN: 大型建筑从主体伸出的那部分
senses.example: The library occupies the east wing of the old palace.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆占了旧宫殿的东侧翼。
senses.why: A side piece spreading out from a body looks like a wing on a bird, so architecture borrowed the word.
senses.whyCN: 从主体伸出去的侧片很像鸟翼，于是建筑也借用了这个词。

senses.title: A group inside a party
senses.definition: one of the groups inside a political party or a movement, holding a distinct view
senses.definitionCN: 政党或运动内部持有不同主张的一组人
senses.example: The moderate wing of the party opposed the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 党内的温和派反对这项新税。
senses.why: A party spreads out on both sides like a pair of wings, and each side got a name of its own.
senses.whyCN: 党派像一对翅膀分向两侧展开，每一侧都得到了自己的名字。

intro.en: Wing is an old Germanic word for the flying limb, related to the verb that meant to flutter; the Norse form had a soft g that eventually fell silent.
intro.cn: wing 是日耳曼语中表示飞行肢体的老词，与意为「扑翅」的动词同源；诺斯语形式的软 g 后来不发音了。

items.en: A common Germanic root named the wing and the act of flapping it.
items.cn: 一个共同的日耳曼词根既指翅膀，也指扑动它的动作。

items.en: The Norse vængr carried a soft g, and this form entered English lands in the north.
items.cn: 诺斯语 vængr 带有软 g，这一形式进入了北方的英格兰地区。

items.en: The native word for wing was feþera, feather, which survived only in the sense of plumage.
items.cn: 古英语本土表示翅膀的词是 feþera（羽毛），只在羽饰义上存活下来。

items.en: The Norse word became the standard wing, and buildings took it for their side parts.
items.cn: 诺斯语词成为标准的 wing，建筑也借它表示侧部。

items.en: Aviation made wing mean the lifting surface, and politics gave each faction a wing of its own.
items.cn: 航空时代让 wing 指升力面，政治又让每个派别各自拥有一翼。

note.en: The first group collects look-alike short words, the second body parts and surfaces with a similar job.
note.cn: 第一组收形近短词，第二组收职司相似的部位与面。

entries.definition: To come out first in a contest.
To complain in a tiresome way.
To move back and forth from a fixed point.

One of the light plates covering a bird.
A thin limb a fish uses to steer.
The side of an animal or an army.

normalIntro.en: Wing is short and ends in a soft -ng, the sound of something spreading out.
normalIntro.cn: wing 很短，收在软的 -ng 上，像东西展开时的声音。

normal.en: The -ng ending hums, like air under a lifted feather.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ng 嗡嗡地响，像羽毛下钻过的空气。

normal.en: Win plus g: you win with a pair of wings, not a single one.
normal.cn: win 加一个 g：靠一对翅膀才赢，单只不够。

normal.en: Swing contains wing, and a wing swings the air.
normal.cn: swing 里含着 wing，翅膀正是把空气拨开的那个东西。

normal.en: A plane wing and a palace wing share the same simple picture: a part sticking out sideways.
normal.cn: 机翼与宫殿侧翼共享同一个简单形象：向侧面伸出去的一块。

normal.en: Under someone's wing is to be sheltered, as chicks under a folded one.
normal.cn: be under someone's wing 是被庇护，就像雏鸟躲在收拢的翼下。

abstract.en: Two shapes unfolding to the full width at once.
abstract.cn: 两个形状在同一瞬间展开到最宽。

abstract.en: The moment after leaving a railing, when no ground is touched.
abstract.cn: 离开栏杆之后、还没碰上任何地面的那一刻。

abstract.en: A shadow passing over a path with no sound attached.
abstract.cn: 一道影子从小径上掠过，却没有附带任何声音。

examples.en: A moth with pale wings knocked against the lamp.
examples.cn: 一只浅色翅膀的蛾子撞在灯上。

examples.en: She was taken under the wing of an older musician.
examples.cn: 她被一位年长的音乐家收在门下。

examples.en: The hospital added a new wing last year.
examples.cn: 医院去年加建了一座侧楼。

dict_mnemonic.text: wing 结尾的 -ng 像翅膀震动时的嗡声。

root: 日耳曼语词根（翼、扑翅）→ 古诺斯语 vængr → 中古英语 winge → wing；同族有 winged、wingless。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a bird's limb, extends to machines of flight, to the sides of buildings, then to the sides of a party.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从鸟的肢体开始，扩展到飞行机械，再到建筑的侧部，最后到党派的阵营。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two feathered shapes unfolded at the moment of take-off.
core.cn: 核心意象：起飞一瞬完全展开的两片羽翼。

branches.en: The bird branch: a white bird rising over the river.
branches.cn: 鸟类分支：白鸟从河面升起。

branches.en: The flying machine branch: ice on the wings of an aircraft.
branches.cn: 飞行器分支：机翼上的冰。

branches.en: The building branch: the east wing of a palace.
branches.cn: 建筑分支：宫殿的东侧翼。

branches.en: The political branch: the moderate wing of a party.
branches.cn: 政治分支：党内的温和派。

branches.en: The shape branch: everything is a part that spreads sideways.
branches.cn: 形状分支：一切都成了向侧面铺开的部分。

intro.en: Wing is a bare Germanic noun that takes common endings and makes compounds such as wingless and wingman.
intro.cn: wing 是光秃的日耳曼名词，能接常见词尾，也能构成 wingless、wingman 这类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The stem has no Latin source; ala, the Latin word for wing, appears only in scientific and borrowed shapes.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语的 ala（翼）只出现在科学与借入的形式里。

items.example: It is the plain noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它既是朴素的动词也是名词。

items.example: The side sense moved into politics.
The picture of chicks under feathers.
items.exampleCN: 雏鸟躲在羽毛下的画面。

definition_zh: 获胜者；得奖者；成功的事物
definition_en: the person or team that comes first in a contest, or a thing that turns out to be a great success
core_image: 领奖台上最高的那一级，那个人低头去接挂上来的奖牌
scene: 颁奖时，最高的那一级台阶上，那个人低头让奖牌挂上脖子，手还在微微发抖。The winner of the spelling contest had never missed a single word.
sceneCN: 这里 winner 是「获胜者」（第 1 个义项：比赛中拿到第一名的人）；句意为拼写比赛的获胜者一个词都没写错。领奖台上低头接奖牌的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 获胜者；得奖者；成功之作

senses.title: The one who comes first
senses.definition: the person or team that finishes ahead of all others in a game or race
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛或竞赛中领先所有人的个人或队伍
senses.example: The winner of the spelling contest had never missed a single word.
senses.exampleCN: 拼写比赛的获胜者一个词都没写错。
senses.why: The ending -er names the doer, so the winner is simply the one who wins.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 命名做事的人，所以 winner 就是那个 win 的人。

senses.title: A person given a prize
senses.definition: a person who receives an award for a work, a piece of writing or a performance
senses.definitionCN: 因作品、文章或表演而获得奖项的人
senses.example: The winner of the essay prize was a girl of fifteen.
senses.exampleCN: 作文奖的得主是一个十五岁的女孩。
senses.why: Not every award comes from a fight, yet the person chosen is still the one who came out on top.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个奖项都来自搏斗，但被选中的人依然是那个拔尖的人。

senses.title: A thing that succeeds
senses.definition: a product, idea or plan that turns out to be very successful
senses.definitionCN: 结果非常成功的产品、想法或方案
senses.example: The new bus service was an immediate winner with commuters.
senses.exampleCN: 新的公交线路立刻受到通勤者的欢迎。
senses.why: People carried the word from persons to things, saying a product won its market just as a runner wins a race.
senses.whyCN: 人们把这个词从人搬到物上，说一个产品赢下了市场，正如跑者赢下比赛。

intro.en: Winner is win plus the doer ending -er, and the base goes back to Old English winnan, to labour and fight.
intro.cn: winner 是 win 加上表施动者的词尾 -er，而词根可回到古英语 winnan（劳作、争斗）。

items.en: winnan meant to struggle and toil, so a winner was first a person who had fought hard.
items.cn: winnan 表示奋斗与劳作，所以 winner 起初指奋力争斗过的人。

items.en: The agent ending -a formed names such as winnend, one who wins.
items.cn: 施动词尾 -a 造出 winnend 之类的名字，意为赢的人。

items.en: The ending became -ere, giving winner, and victory in games came to the front.
items.cn: 词尾变为 -ere，形成 winner，游戏中的取胜义走到了前面。

items.en: Sports reporting fixed the word for the first-place person or team.
items.cn: 体育报道把这个词固定给第一名的个人或队伍。

items.en: Advertisers extended it to products and ideas, so a bus route could be a winner too.
items.cn: 广告人又把它扩展到产品与想法，于是一条公交线路也能是赢家。

note.en: The first group collects members of the same family, the second other names for the person who comes first.
note.cn: 第一组收同族成员，第二组收其他指第一名的称呼。

entries.definition: The verb behind the person.
Money gained from a bet or a game.
The coldest of the seasons.
Belonging to the winner in a possessive form.
The overall best in a sport, often holding a title.
A formal word for the one who defeats another.
The one who comes last instead of first.

normalIntro.en: Winner is one of the easiest family members: win plus the -er that means the person who does it.
normalIntro.cn: winner 是最容易记的词族成员之一：win 加上表示「做此事的人」的 -er。

normal.en: Win plus er, the same -er as in teacher and worker.
normal.cn: win 加 er，与 teacher、worker 里的 -er 一样。

normal.en: Double n is kept from win before the ending.
normal.cn: 加词尾前保留了 win 的两个 n。

normal.en: The -ner ending sounds like the last syllable of dinner, a prize meal.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ner 听起来像 dinner 的末音节，像一顿庆功饭。

normal.en: Winnings is the money, winner is the person: one letter more, one meaning more.
normal.cn: winnings 是钱，winner 是人：多一个字母，多一层意思。

normal.en: A winner is not always first; sometimes it is the product everyone buys.
normal.cn: winner 不一定永远是第一名，有时是人人都在买的产品。

abstract.en: A medal lowered over a bowed head.
abstract.cn: 奖牌从上方挂向低下的头。

abstract.en: A name called out and a silence just after it.
abstract.cn: 名字被念出来之后那一小段安静。

abstract.en: The feeling inside a hand that will not stop shaking.
abstract.cn: 一只停不下颤抖的手里的感受。

examples.en: The winner received a cup and a small cheque.
examples.cn: 获胜者得到一只奖杯和一张小支票。

examples.en: Nobody was surprised when she was announced as the winner.
examples.cn: 宣布她是获胜者时，没人感到惊讶。

examples.en: The design was a winner from the first day in the shops.
examples.cn: 这个设计从上市第一天起就是赢家。

dict_mnemonic.text: win（赢）+ er（人）—— 赢的那个人，就是「获胜者」。

root: 古英语 winnan（奋斗、争得）→ win → win + -er → winner；同族有 winning、winnings、win。

sensesIntro.en: A hard fighter becomes the first-place person, then the receiver of a prize, and finally any thing that succeeds.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个奋力争斗的人，先成为第一名，再成为领奖的人，最后成了任何成功的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the highest step of the platform, a bowed head.
core.cn: 核心意象：领奖台最高的那一级，低下去的头。

branches.en: The contest branch: a spelling champion with no mistakes.
branches.cn: 竞赛分支：一个错字都没有的拼写冠军。

branches.en: The award branch: a fifteen-year-old essay winner.
branches.cn: 奖项分支：一个十五岁的作文奖得主。

branches.en: The product branch: a bus route that commuters love.
branches.cn: 产品分支：通勤者喜爱的公交线路。

branches.en: The person branch: the doer of the verb, now wearing a medal.
branches.cn: 人物分支：动词的施动者，如今挂着奖牌。

branches.en: The evaluation branch: a winner is whatever others decide to honour.
branches.cn: 评价分支：赢家是别人决定要表彰的那一个。

intro.en: Winner is a transparent piece of word building: the root win plus the agent suffix -er.
intro.cn: winner 是构造极透明的词：词根 win 加上施动词尾 -er。

latinIntro.en: Neither the root nor the suffix is Latin here; the Latin entry is only a borrowed synonym.
latinIntro.cn: 这里的词根与词尾都不是拉丁语；拉丁条目只是借入的同义词。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 winners 与 winnings。

items.meaning: the one who does not win
items.exampleCN: 同一构词法用在 lose 上。
这个词进入了经济领域。

definition_zh: 冬天；冬季；寒冷的时期；（引申）低谷期
definition_en: the coldest season of the year, and by extension a cold or unproductive period of life or business
core_image: 光秃的树枝上挂着薄冰，地上只剩一层硬硬的霜，呼出的气白成一团
scene: 河面结了薄冰，光秃的树枝上挂着霜，人一出门呼出的气就白成一团。Snow lay on the fields all winter long.
sceneCN: 这里 winter 是「冬天」（第 1 个义项：一年中最冷的季节）；句意为整个冬天田野上都覆着雪。结冰的河面和树上那层霜，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The cold season
senses.definition: the season between autumn and spring, the coldest part of the year, with short days
senses.definitionCN: 秋冬之间的季节，一年中最冷、白昼最短的时期
senses.example: Snow lay on the fields all winter long.
senses.exampleCN: 整个冬天田野上都覆着雪。
senses.why: The oldest meaning is simply the wet or cold season, named long before calendars were fixed.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是寒冷潮湿的季节，早在历法确定之前就已得名。

senses.title: A time of cold weather
senses.definition: very cold weather, or a period when such weather lasts unusually long
senses.definitionCN: 极冷的天气，或这类天气持续得特别长的一段时间
senses.example: The farm lost half its sheep in that terrible winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那个可怕的寒季，农场损失了一半的羊。
senses.why: Because the season is defined by its cold, the word can stand for the cold itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个季节以寒冷为标志，这个词也能直接代指寒冷本身。

senses.title: A fallow or hard period
senses.definition: a period when activity, growth or fortune is low, as in the winter of a business or a life
senses.definitionCN: 活力、增长或运势低落的时期，如生意或人生的冬天
senses.example: The company survived the winter of the crisis and grew again.
senses.exampleCN: 公司熬过了危机的冬天，又重新生长。
senses.why: Bare trees and empty fields look like loss, so people use the season for any time of decline.
senses.whyCN: 光秃的树与空空的田野看起来像失去，于是人们用这个季节指任何衰退的时期。

intro.en: Winter is a common Germanic season word built on the same root as wet and wind, naming the wet or snowy half of the year.
intro.cn: winter 是日耳曼语共有的季节词，与 wet、wind 同根，命名一年中潮湿多雪的那一半。

items.en: A root with the sense of wet or white time gave the peoples of the north a name for the cold season.
items.cn: 一个带有潮湿、洁白意味的词根，给了北方各族命名寒冷季节的词。

items.en: winter was both a noun and a verb, and the year was often counted in winters.
items.cn: winter 既是名词也是动词，人们常用「几个冬天」来计算年岁。

items.en: The word kept its shape while spelling changed little, and wintry joined it as an adjective.
items.cn: 这个词形式基本未变，拼写改动不大，形容词 wintry 也加入进来。

items.en: Calendars fixed the season to three months, and winter clothes and winter sports grew as its company.
items.cn: 历法把这个季节固定为三个月，冬衣与冬季运动成了它的同伴。

items.en: Modern writing borrowed the season for hard times, as in the winter of a career.
items.cn: 现代写作把这个季节借给艰难时期，如事业之冬。

note.en: The first group holds the other seasons and look-alikes, the second words for cold and for hard periods.
note.cn: 第一组收其他季节与形近词，第二组收表示寒冷与艰难时期的词。

entries.definition: The one who comes first.
Twisting from side to side.
The warmest season, its opposite.
The season just before winter.
A cold feeling in the air or the body.
A thin white coat of ice on surfaces.
A period of falling strength or success.

normalIntro.en: Winter shares its opening with wind and wet, which is exactly the weather it names.
normalIntro.cn: winter 与 wind、wet 开头相同，而那正是它所命名的天气。

normal.en: Wind and wet both begin like winter, and both belong to it.
normal.cn: wind 和 wet 都以 winter 的方式开头，也都属于它。

normal.en: The -ter ending appears in other periods too, such as the word for the end of an age.
normal.cn: 结尾的 -ter 也出现在其他时段词里，比如表示某种终了岁月的词。

normal.en: The middle i is thin and sharp, like cold air.
normal.cn: 中间的 i 又细又尖，像冷空气。

normal.en: Add a y and you get wintry, cold and bare.
normal.cn: 加一个 y 就得到 wintry，寒冷而光秃。

normal.en: Remember the old habit of counting age in winters: twenty winters meant twenty years.
normal.cn: 记得古人用「几个冬天」计岁：二十个冬天就是二十岁。

abstract.en: Breath turning white and disappearing at once.
abstract.cn: 呼出的气变白，随即消失。

abstract.en: A river holding still under a thin hard skin.
abstract.cn: 河流停在一层又薄又硬的皮下面。

abstract.en: Bare branches writing dark lines on grey sky.
abstract.cn: 光秃的枝条在灰天上写出黑色的线。

examples.en: We spent the whole winter in the mountains.
examples.cn: 我们在山里度过了整个冬天。

examples.en: Winter comes early in the north of the country.
examples.cn: 这个国家的北方，冬天来得早。

examples.en: The shop closes early in winter.
examples.cn: 这家店在冬天早早就关门。

dict_mnemonic.text: wind（风）+ wet（湿）合起来的感觉，就是「冬天」。

root: 日耳曼语 season 词根（潮湿、寒冷，与 wet、wind 同源）→ 古英语 winter → winter；同族有 wintry、winterize。

sensesIntro.en: From the cold wet half of the year the word widens to cold weather itself, then becomes a picture for any season of hardship.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一年中寒冷潮湿的一半，扩展到寒冷天气本身，再变成一切艰难时节的图画。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bare branches over a river frozen thin.
core.cn: 核心意象：结着薄冰的河面上方那些光秃的枝条。

branches.en: The calendar branch: snow lying on the fields all season.
branches.cn: 历法分支：整个季节田野上都覆着雪。

branches.en: The weather branch: a terrible winter that took the sheep.
branches.cn: 天气分支：夺走羊群的可怕寒冬。

branches.en: The metaphor branch: a company crossing the crisis.
branches.cn: 隐喻分支：公司穿过危机之冬。

branches.en: The bare branch: trees stripped, work stopped.
branches.cn: 萧瑟分支：树被剥光，活也停摆。

branches.en: The hardship branch: cold becomes a name for loss.
branches.cn: 艰难分支：寒冷成了失去的名字。

intro.en: Winter takes the adjective ending -y for wintry and appears inside compounds such as wintertime and midwinter.
intro.cn: winter 能接形容词词尾 -y 变成 wintry，也出现在 wintertime、midwinter 这类复合词里。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin entry shows how another language named the same season.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于日耳曼语；拉丁条目展示另一种语言如何命名同一个季节。

items.example: It stands alone as noun, verb and modifier.
items.exampleCN: 它单独充当名词、动词和修饰语。

items.example: The season named twice at once.
items.exampleCN: 季节被同时命名了两次。

items.meaning: a sport played on snow or ice

definition_zh: 擦；擦净；抹去；（引申）消除；抹掉
definition_en: to clean or dry a surface by passing a cloth or the hand over it, and to remove something in that motion
core_image: 一只手拿着湿布从桌子一端抹到另一端，水痕和 crumbs 一起被推到桌角
scene: 饭后，他把湿布往桌上一铺，从这头抹到那头，汤渍和碎屑一起被推到桌角。She wiped the table twice before the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 wipe 是「擦、擦净」（第 1 个义项：用布或手在表面抹过使之洁净）；句意为客人到达前她把桌子擦了两遍。湿布从桌子一头推到另一头那道弧线，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To clean a surface
senses.definition: to pass a cloth over a surface to clean or dry it
senses.definitionCN: 用布在表面抹过，使之干净或干燥
senses.example: She wiped the table twice before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到达前她把桌子擦了两遍。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a single sweeping movement of the hand over something, and cleaning came with it.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是手在某物上一道抹过，洁净之义随这道动作而来。

senses.title: To remove by rubbing
senses.definition: to take something off a surface with a cloth or the hand, such as liquid, dust or tears
senses.definitionCN: 用布或手把液体、灰尘或眼泪从表面上带走
senses.example: He wiped the mud off his boots at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门口把靴子上的泥擦掉。
senses.why: Once the movement cleans, the thing carried away becomes the point: what is wiped is gone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这道动作能清洁，被带走的东西就成了重点：被擦掉的就是没了。

senses.title: To destroy completely
senses.definition: in phrases such as wipe out, to remove something entirely, sometimes with great violence
senses.definitionCN: 在 wipe out 等说法中，指把某物完全除去，有时指猛烈毁灭
senses.example: The flood wiped out the village's only bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水冲毁了村里唯一的一座桥。
senses.why: If a cloth can make a mark disappear, then a force can make a whole thing disappear in the same image.
senses.whyCN: 既然一块布能让痕迹消失，那么一股力量也能用同样的画面让整个东西消失。

senses.title: The act of wiping
senses.definition: a single movement with a cloth, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 用布抹一次的动作，作可数名词
senses.example: A quick wipe with a dry cloth will do.
senses.exampleCN: 用干布快速擦一下就行。
senses.why: The noun simply names the movement that the verb performs.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是命名动词所做的那个动作。

intro.en: Wipe is a Germanic word of movement, first recorded in Old English as wipian, to rub or clean a surface.
intro.cn: wipe 是日耳曼语中表示动作的词，古英语里最先记为 wipian，意为擦、拭净表面。

items.en: wipian meant to rub or wipe something clean, often with a cloth.
items.cn: wipian 表示摩擦或把某物擦净，常用布来做。

items.en: The word kept the same body but gained the phrasal partners off and away.
items.cn: 这个词形式未变，却获得了 off、away 这样的介词伙伴。

items.en: To wipe away tears appears early, extending the verb from objects to the face.
items.cn: 擦去眼泪的用法很早就出现，把这个动词从物件扩展到了脸。

items.en: Wipe out, meaning to destroy utterly, spread through war reporting and later sport.
items.cn: 表示彻底摧毁的 wipe out 通过战地报道传播，后来又进入体育。

items.en: Cleaners and machines gave the noun new life, from windscreen wipers to wet wipes.
items.cn: 清洁用品与机器给名词带来新生命，从雨刷到湿纸巾。

note.en: The first group holds short look-alikes, the second verbs of cleaning and removing.
note.cn: 第一组收形近短词，第二组收表示清洁与除去的动词。

entries.definition: Broad from side to side.
A thin thread of metal.
A drink made from grapes.
A blade that sweeps a windscreen.
To remove dirt from something.
To move the hand firmly over a surface.
To remove marks or data completely.

normalIntro.en: Wipe is a single short movement, so say it aloud while moving your hand across a table.
normalIntro.cn: wipe 就一个短动作，念它的时候顺手在桌上抹一下，就记住了。

normal.en: The w at the start is the shape of the cloth folding as you push it.
normal.cn: 开头的 w 像你推布时布面折起的形状。

normal.en: The silent e at the end keeps the i long, as in wide and white.
normal.cn: 末尾不发音的 e 让 i 保持长音，和 wide、white 一样。

normal.en: The past is wiped, not wipeed: drop the e before -ed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wiped 而不是 wipeed：加 -ed 前要去掉 e。

normal.en: Add out and the cloth becomes a flood: wipe out.
normal.cn: 加上 out，布就变成了洪水：wipe out。

normal.en: A wiper is the same motion made by a machine on a windscreen.
normal.cn: wiper 是同样的动作，由机器在挡风玻璃上完成。

abstract.en: Water and crumbs pushed into a single line at the table edge.
abstract.cn: 水和碎屑被推到桌边，排成一条线。

abstract.en: A sleeve doing what a cloth should do.
abstract.cn: 袖子干了布该干的活。

abstract.en: A mark on a window that is there and then suddenly is not.
abstract.cn: 窗上的一道痕迹，在，然后忽然不在。

examples.en: Wipe your feet before you come in.
examples.cn: 进来之前把脚擦一擦。

examples.en: She wiped her eyes with the back of her hand.
examples.cn: 她用手背擦了擦眼睛。

examples.en: The storm wiped out the whole harvest in one night.
examples.cn: 一场风暴一夜之间毁掉了整季收成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 念 wipe 时手心朝下往外一抹，就是「擦」的动作。

root: 古英语 wipian（擦拭、抹净）→ 中古英语 wipen → wipe；同族有 wiper、wipeout、wet wipe。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as one sweep of the hand, narrows to the thing carried away, then widens to total destruction, and finally names the movement itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从手的一道抹擦开始，收窄到被带走的东西，再扩展到彻底毁灭，最后命名这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet cloth crossing a table in one sweep.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块湿布从桌子这头抹到那头。

branches.en: The cleaning branch: a table wiped twice before guests.
branches.cn: 清洁分支：客人来前擦了两遍的桌子。

branches.en: The removal branch: mud taken off boots at the door.
branches.cn: 除去分支：门口擦掉的靴上泥。

branches.en: The destruction branch: a bridge gone with the flood.
branches.cn: 毁灭分支：随洪水消失的桥。

branches.en: The noun branch: one quick pass with a dry cloth.
branches.cn: 名词分支：用干布快速抹一下。

branches.en: The vanishing branch: what is wiped leaves no mark behind.
branches.cn: 消失分支：被擦掉的不会留下痕迹。

intro.en: Wipe takes ordinary verb endings and builds compounds such as wipeout and the noun wiper.
intro.cn: wipe 能接普通动词词尾，也能构成 wipeout 与名词 wiper。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entry is a borrowed synonym.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁条目只是借入的同义词。

items.meaning: the one or the tool that wipes

definition_zh: 金属丝；电线；（电）电报；铁丝网；汇款
definition_en: a thin thread of metal, especially one carrying electric current, and by extension a telegram or a money transfer
core_image: 一只灰色的盒子背后垂出几根细金属线，指尖一碰有点发麻
scene: 拆开旧收音机，里面盘着几根细金属线，螺丝一松就弹了出来。A loose wire behind the desk was the cause of the short circuit.
sceneCN: 这里 wire 是「电线、金属丝」（第 1 个义项：细细的一根金属线）；句意为桌子后面一根松了的电线导致了短路。盒子里盘着的那几根细线，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 金属丝；电线；电报；铁丝网

collocations.zh: 带电的电线；精力充沛的人

senses.title: A thin thread of metal
senses.definition: a long thin piece of metal, often bendable, used for holding, shaping or carrying current
senses.definitionCN: 细长可弯的金属条，用来固定、造型或导电
senses.example: The basket was made of thin copper wire.
senses.exampleCN: 这只篮子是用细铜丝编成的。
senses.why: The earliest sense is the drawn metal itself, a thread that could be bent into any shape.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是拉制出来的金属本身，一根可以弯成任何形状的线。

senses.title: A conductor of electricity
senses.definition: a metal thread covered with plastic that carries electric current in a building or a machine
senses.definitionCN: 外面包着塑料的金属线，在建筑或机器中输送电流
senses.example: A loose wire behind the desk was the cause of the short circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 桌子后面一根松了的电线导致了短路。
senses.why: Once electric current travelled along drawn metal, the thread of the craftsman became the artery of a house.
senses.whyCN: 电流开始沿着拉制金属走，工匠的那根线就成了房屋的血管。

senses.title: A telegram or a money transfer
senses.definition: a message sent along telegraph wires, or money sent between banks by message rather than in person
senses.definitionCN: 沿电报线发出的讯息，或银行之间以讯息而非现金方式转账的钱
senses.example: The news came by wire from the capital that same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 当晚消息就从首都用电报发了过来。
senses.why: Both messages and money moved along the wire, so the wire itself became the name of the service.
senses.whyCN: 消息和钱都沿着这条线走，于是线本身成了这项业务的名字。

senses.title: To install electric wiring
senses.definition: to fit a building or a device with the wires that carry power or signals
senses.definitionCN: 给建筑或设备装上输电或传信号的线路
senses.example: They wired the old house before moving in.
senses.exampleCN: 搬进去之前他们给老房子装了电线。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb, meaning to provide a thing with this new kind of thread.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成动词，意为给某物配上这种新的线。

intro.en: Wire comes from Old English wir, the name of drawn metal worked into jewellery; the electrical sense arrived only in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: wire 来自古英语 wir，是拉制金属、用于制作首饰的名称；与电有关的义项到十九世纪才出现。

items.en: wir named fine drawn metal, used in rings and boxes rather than in machines.
items.cn: wir 指拉制得很细的金属，用于戒指与盒饰，而不是机器。

items.en: The word widened to bowls, strings and instruments, where a thread of metal holds or sings.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到碗、弦与乐器：一根金属线用来系住或发声。

items.en: The telegraph spread the word along its own lines, and a telegram became a wire.
items.cn: 电报让自己的线路把这个词传播开来，一封电报就被称作 wire。

items.en: Electric power gave wire its modern centre: the plastic-coated thread inside every wall.
items.cn: 电力给了 wire 现代的核心义：每一面墙里那根包着塑料的线。

items.en: Banks and later broadcasters produced wire transfers and wireless signals.
items.cn: 银行以及后来的广播人又造出了电汇与无线信号。

note.en: The first group holds look-alikes formed from adjacent letters, the second cables and threads of metal.
note.cn: 第一组收字母相近的形近词，第二组收电缆与金属线。

entries.definition: To clean with one sweep of a cloth.
Broad from one side to the other.
To pay for the use of something.
Thin and strong, like wire.
A thick bundle of wires or fibres.
A thin line of fibre, the picture behind wire.
A very thin strand of material.

normalIntro.en: Wire is short and thin like the thing itself, and its silent e keeps the long i.
normalIntro.cn: wire 像它所指之物一样短而细，末尾的 e 让 i 保持长音。

normal.en: Five letters, all narrow: the word looks like a wire on the page.
normal.cn: 五个字母一个比一个窄，这个词在纸上就像一根线。

normal.en: The silent e keeps the i long, as in fire and hire.
normal.cn: 不发音的 e 保持 i 长音，如 fire、hire。

normal.en: Wiry means thin and strong, so a wiry runner is built like wire.
normal.cn: wiry 意为瘦而结实，所以 a wiry runner 就像金属丝一样的人。

normal.en: Wireless drops the wire: signals travel without it.
normal.cn: wireless 去掉那根 wire：信号不再需要它。

normal.en: A telegram travelled on wires, so in old films a wire is a message.
normal.cn: 电报沿着电线走，所以老电影里 a wire 就是一封电文。

abstract.en: A faint hum heard through the box before it is opened.
abstract.cn: 盒子还没打开，就从里面听见一点嗡声。

abstract.en: A thread of copper catching a single point of light.
abstract.cn: 一根铜丝接住了一个光点。

abstract.en: A jump in the fingertip when the screwdriver touches the wrong spot.
abstract.cn: 螺丝刀碰到不该碰的地方时，指尖一跳。

examples.en: The fence is made of wire and wooden posts.
examples.cn: 这道篱笆由金属丝和木桩做成。

examples.en: Do not touch that wire with wet hands.
examples.cn: 不要用湿手碰那根电线。

examples.en: He wired the money to his brother the same afternoon.
examples.cn: 当天下午他就把钱电汇给了弟弟。

dict_mnemonic.text: fire 换成 w 开头，暖与光变成了细细的「电线、金属丝」。

root: 古英语 wir（拉制的细金属）→ 中古英语 wyr/wire → wire；同族有 wiring、wireless、wiretap。

sensesIntro.en: A drawn thread of metal becomes the carrier of electricity, then a channel for messages and money, and finally a verb of fitting such lines.
sensesIntro.cn: 一根拉制的金属线成为电的载体，再成为消息与金钱的通道，最后变成安装这种线路的动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bright thread of copper bending in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯在手里的细亮铜丝。

branches.en: The metal branch: a basket woven from copper wire.
branches.cn: 金属分支：用铜丝编成的篮子。

branches.en: The current branch: a loose wire behind the desk.
branches.cn: 电流分支：桌后松了的电线。

branches.en: The message branch: news arriving by telegraph.
branches.cn: 消息分支：用电报传来的新闻。

branches.en: The verb branch: an old house fitted with lines.
branches.cn: 动词分支：给老房子装线。

branches.en: The carrier branch: whatever travels quickly takes the line's name.
branches.cn: 载体分支：走得快的东西都借用了线的名字。

intro.en: Wire takes simple endings and forms a rich family: wiring, wireless and the compound barbed wire.
intro.cn: wire 能接简单词尾，构成丰富的一族：wiring、wireless 以及复合词 barbed wire。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Old English; the Latin entry is a borrowed word for a metal thread.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词干属于古英语；拉丁条目只是借入的表示金属线的词。

definition_zh: 智慧；明智；学问；（前人的）经验之谈
definition_en: the ability to judge well and act sensibly, gained through knowledge and long experience
core_image: 老人坐在院里的树下，听完年轻人的问题，沉默了一会儿才慢慢开口
scene: 老人听完那个难题，先笑了，又沉默了一会儿才慢慢开口，一句话把纷乱理清。She had the wisdom to say nothing until everyone had spoken.
sceneCN: 这里 wisdom 是「智慧」（第 1 个义项：判断得当、行事合理的能力）；句意为她很有智慧，等所有人都说完才开口。老人在树下先沉默再开口的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 智慧；明智；学问；经验之谈

senses.title: Good judgement from experience
senses.definition: the ability to make sound judgements, built from knowledge and years of experience
senses.definitionCN: 做出稳妥判断的能力，由知识与多年经验积累而成
senses.example: She had the wisdom to say nothing until everyone had spoken.
senses.exampleCN: 她很有智慧，等所有人都说完才开口。
senses.why: The ending -dom names a state, as in freedom and kingdom, so wisdom is the state of being wise.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -dom 命名一种状态，如 freedom、kingdom，所以 wisdom 就是处于明智的状态。

senses.title: Knowledge stored in books
senses.definition: the collected learning of a civilisation, often the sayings and books of the past
senses.definitionCN: 一个文明积存的学识，常指往昔的格言与典籍
senses.example: The library keeps the wisdom of three thousand years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座图书馆收藏着三千年的学问。
senses.why: When judgement is written down, it becomes a body of knowledge that later readers can inherit.
senses.whyCN: 当判断被写下来，它就成了一部可供后来者承继的知识。

senses.title: What most people believe
senses.definition: in phrases such as conventional wisdom, the opinion that is widely accepted, whether right or wrong
senses.definitionCN: 在 conventional wisdom 等说法中，指被广泛接受的看法，对错不论
senses.example: Conventional wisdom said the shop could never survive in a village.
senses.exampleCN: 通行看法认为这家店在村里绝无生路。
senses.why: The word keeps a slight irony here: the wisdom of the many is only a belief they share.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词带一点反讽：众人的智慧，只是众人共有的相信。

intro.en: Wisdom joins the adjective wise to the old suffix -dom, a Germanic ending that turns a quality into a state, as in kingdom.
intro.cn: wisdom 把形容词 wise 与古词尾 -dom 相连，这个日耳曼语词尾把品质变成状态，如 kingdom。

items.en: wīsdōm was a compound of wīs, wise, and dōm, judgement or decree.
items.cn: wīsdōm 是 wīs（明智的）与 dōm（判断、裁定）的复合词。

items.en: Because dōm meant judgement rather than a mere state, the word first stressed the act of deciding well.
items.cn: 由于 dōm 意为判断而非单纯状态，这个词起初强调的是判断得宜这一行为。

items.en: The compound settled as wisdom, and came to mean the learning of the old and the sages.
items.cn: 复合词固定为 wisdom，进而指老人与贤者的学识。

items.en: Books of wisdom, especially in the Bible, gave the word a lasting link with written teaching.
items.cn: 智慧书，尤其圣经中的智慧书，让这个词与书面教诲结下长久联系。

items.en: Conventional wisdom and wisdom tooth show the word widening to shared opinion and to the late tooth.
items.cn: conventional wisdom 与 wisdom tooth 显示这个词扩展到共同看法与那颗迟来的牙。

note.en: The first group collects words built with -dom or the same stem, the second covers other names for good judgement.
note.cn: 第一组收以 -dom 或以同一词干构成的词，第二组收其他表示良好判断的称呼。

entries.definition: The adjective that stands behind it.
In a sensible, careful way.
The state of being free.
A country ruled by a king or queen.
Facts and understanding gathered over time.
A deep and clear understanding of a problem.
Foolish behaviour that shows no judgement.

normalIntro.en: Wisdom is wise plus -dom, so it names the state of being wise, not a person who is wise.
normalIntro.cn: wisdom 是 wise 加 -dom，命名的是明智的状态，而不是某个明智的人。

normal.en: The ending -dom also builds kingdom and freedom: states of being.
normal.cn: 词尾 -dom 也构成 kingdom、freedom：都是某种状态。

normal.en: The i in wise shortens in wisdom: wide becomes width the same way.
normal.cn: wise 的 i 在 wisdom 里变短，wide 变 width 也是同理。

normal.en: Wisdom is knowledge plus time, so picture grey hair rather than a book.
normal.cn: 智慧是知识加上时间，所以要想灰白的头发，而不是一本书。

normal.en: A wisdom tooth arrives late, just as judgement arrives later than teeth.
normal.cn: 智齿来得晚，正如判断比牙齿来得更晚。

normal.en: Conventional wisdom is the wisdom of the crowd, often right and sometimes wrong.
normal.cn: conventional wisdom 是众人的智慧，常常对，有时也错。

abstract.en: A long pause before a short answer.
abstract.cn: 一个长停顿之后的那句短话。

abstract.en: A hand held up to stop a young man from rushing.
abstract.cn: 一只举起的手，拦住要冲出去的年轻人。

abstract.en: Quiet in a room where everyone else is certain.
abstract.cn: 满屋人都很确定时，那份安静。

examples.en: Age had given him patience rather than wisdom.
examples.cn: 年岁给他的更多是耐心而不是智慧。

examples.en: It is not wisdom to borrow money for a holiday.
examples.cn: 为了度假借钱，不算明智。

examples.en: The book gathers the wisdom of farmers across four generations.
examples.cn: 这本书汇集了四代农人的经验之谈。

dict_mnemonic.text: wise（明智的）+ dom（状态）—— 明智的状态，就是「智慧」。

root: 古英语 wīs（明智的）+ dōm（判断、裁定）→ wīsdōm → wisdom；同族有 wise、wisely、unwise。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as good judgement, then becomes the accumulated learning of the past, and finally the everyday beliefs people share.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从良好的判断开始，成为往昔积累的学识，最后成了人们共有的日常看法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old man silent under a tree before he speaks.
core.cn: 核心意象：树下沉默良久才开口的老人。

branches.en: The judgement branch: saying nothing until all have spoken.
branches.cn: 判断分支：等所有人说完才开口。

branches.en: The learning branch: three thousand years on the shelves.
branches.cn: 学识分支：书架上三千年的积累。

branches.en: The belief branch: the crowd's opinion about the shop.
branches.cn: 看法分支：众人对那家店的判断。

branches.en: The irony branch: shared belief is not always wise.
branches.cn: 反讽分支：共有的看法并不总是明智。

branches.en: The inheritance branch: what one age hands to the next.
branches.cn: 传承分支：一个时代交给下一个时代的东西。

intro.en: Wisdom is a Germanic compound of wise and the state suffix -dom; the same suffix appears in freedom and kingdom.
intro.cn: wisdom 是 wise 与状态词尾 -dom 组成的日耳曼语复合词；同样的词尾出现在 freedom、kingdom 里。

latinIntro.en: The word is native, with no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below are borrowed cousins for the same idea.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土词，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁条目只是表达同一观念的借入表亲。

items.example: The adjective the noun grows from.
items.exampleCN: 名词所由生长的形容词。

items.example: Latness named by the same idea.
items.exampleCN: 迟来之物借用同一观念命名。
